assessment.nobel_worthiness: Aberration correction in the electron microscope removed the spherical-aberration limit that held resolution back for decades. It is a clear, original instrumental invention that opened the door to atom-by-atom imaging and spectroscopy of interfaces, defects, catalysts and 2D materials. It is the kind of tool-driven discovery the prize has honoured before, and I know its impact first-hand from my own field.
assessment.attribution: Rose supplied the theoretical corrector designs, Haider led the hexapole corrector realisation, and Urban led the first demonstrations of sub-angstrom imaging with Haider. Together they make a fair three-person configuration. Other pioneers such as Ondrej Krivanek (quadrupole-octupole correctors, STEM) are not in the credited names, so the historical record needs checking before a prize configuration is settled.
assessment.maturity: Mature. Correctors have been routine in commercial instruments for over fifteen years, with many independent confirmations and thousands of results. Recognition is not premature and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Krivanek and the STEM corrector lineage are outside the supplied credit and could change the fair allocation of credit.
Possible concern that the prize would look like a methods prize for a single community, though the cross-field impact is large.
I rely on my own recollection of the corrector history and have not verified the dates of the first demonstrations.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental observation of the Higgs boson in 2012 confirmed the mechanism of electroweak symmetry breaking. It is a verified, unambiguous discovery of the first fundamental scalar, and it has been confirmed by two independent experiments and by a decade of property measurements. It matters directly for our understanding of nature.
assessment.attribution: The 2013 prize went to the theorists. For the experimental side the decisive contributions are the conception and leadership of ATLAS and CMS, and the credit is spread over thousands of people. A three-person prize naturally points to the founding spokespersons and key conceivers of the two detectors, namely Jenni and Della Negra and Virdee. Gianotti, spokesperson at the time of the announcement, is an equally strong claim, so the choice among four is uncertain and contentious.
assessment.maturity: Very mature. Two independent experiments, repeated measurements of couplings and spin-parity, and more than a decade since the discovery.
uncertainties: Selecting three from four credited names is a judgement that may be seen as unfair to Gianotti.
The collaboration nature of the work conflicts with the statutes' limit of three persons and the 'original experimenters' principle.
The relation to the 2013 theory prize may be read as completing rather than opening a topic.
Details of individual leadership roles are from memory and not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, based on Katori's magic-wavelength concept, reach fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and have transformed precision metrology, tests of fundamental physics, relativistic geodesy and the road to a redefinition of the second. It is a clear invention with a verified realisation and wide impact.
assessment.attribution: Katori invented the magic-wavelength lattice clock concept and made the first demonstration. Ye realised the most accurate implementations and extended them into many-body clocks and precision spectroscopy. This is a clean two-person configuration. Comparisons with the earlier Hall and Haensch prize for frequency combs and ion-clock work (Wineland) must be considered.
assessment.maturity: Mature. Multiple groups across the world, intercomparisons between clocks, and agreement at the 1e-18 level. The redefinition of the second is pending, but the science is well established.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier prizes on frequency combs and trapped-ion control may weigh on novelty.
Other contributors to lattice-clock theory and strontium and ytterbium implementations might be argued for.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The IceCube observation of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos in 2013, followed by evidence of a source in TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane, opened a new window on the universe. It required building a cubic-kilometre detector in the Antarctic ice, so it combines instrumentation and discovery.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led the IceCube concept, Karle was central to the detector construction and early analysis, and Spiering was a key figure in the AMANDA and IceCube collaboration. The collaboration is large and the 'original' roles are shared with other founders, so the allocation is not obvious.
assessment.maturity: Fairly mature. The diffuse flux is confirmed by several channels and independently supported by ANTARES and Baikal-GVD at lower significance. Source identification is still developing.
uncertainties: The sources of the neutrinos are largely unresolved, which limits the astrophysical understanding.
Attribution among AMANDA, Baikal and IceCube pioneers is uncertain.
Details of individual roles are from memory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theory of flat bands at the magic angle and the experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene created the field of moire quantum matter. It is a fresh, original and very influential discovery with a tunable platform that many other materials followed.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the flat bands in 2011, and Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive 2018 experimental observations. This is a natural three-person theory-plus-experiment configuration. Others, notably Cory Dean and Kim, and Yacoby, contributed to the follow-up, and Lopes dos Santos et al. earlier flagged related band flattening, which may complicate the credit.
assessment.maturity: Moderately mature. Replicated by many independent groups, but the origin of the superconductivity and the interpretation of the correlated phases are still debated. The recognition may be early but not unreasonable.
uncertainties: The mechanism of superconductivity remains unresolved.
Priority questions about earlier theory work on twisted bilayers.
Sample-dependent behaviour has complicated reproducibility in some reports.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Giant tunnel magnetoresistance in crystalline MgO junctions turned magnetic tunnel junctions into a practical technology, behind hard-disk read heads and MRAM. It combines a verified experimental discovery with a predictive theory of spin-filtering, and it affects daily life.
assessment.attribution: Yuasa and Parkin demonstrated large room-temperature TMR in epitaxial and textured MgO junctions in 2004, independently and almost simultaneously, and Butler (with Mathon and Umerski) predicted the coherent tunnelling effect. The theory credit is shared, and Mathon and Umerski are not in the supplied credit. Fair attribution is disputed.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with extensive industrial adoption and independent confirmation. The 2007 prize for GMR (Fert and Gruenberg) is closely related and may reduce the perceived novelty.
uncertainties: Close relationship to the GMR prize.
Theory credit for Mathon and Umerski is outside the supplied names.
Simultaneous independent discoveries by Yuasa and Parkin complicate the priority record.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators combine the theory of the quantum spin Hall effect with the experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells and the later quantum anomalous Hall effect in magnetic topological insulator films. The experiments verify a new state of matter and open prospects for dissipationless edge transport.
assessment.attribution: Kane (with Mele) formulated the theory, Molenkamp's group measured the quantum spin Hall edge conductance in 2007, and Xue's group observed the quantum anomalous Hall effect in 2013. These are different parts of a compound discovery, and Mele, Bernevig, Zhang and Konig are outside this list's names or are not credited, so the allocation is awkward.
assessment.maturity: Mature in basic confirmation, with many independent reproductions. Applications remain limited and the 2016 prize on topological phases lowers the margin for a further topological prize.
uncertainties: The compound nature of the discovery means different parts need different recognition.
Credit of Zhang, Bernevig and Mele is not captured by this entry.
Overlap with the 2016 prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The first horizon-scale images of M87* and Sgr A* give direct visual evidence of black-hole shadows and test general relativity in the strong-field regime. It is a technical achievement in very-long-baseline interferometry and a compelling observational result.
assessment.attribution: The EHT is a collaboration of hundreds, so a prize to individuals is hard. Doeleman led the project and the VLBI development and Falcke proposed the shadow concept and led the science case, with Zensus as a founding figure. The honest assessment is that the original roles are diffused, which conflicts with the committee's wish to identify the people who did the original work.
assessment.maturity: Moderately mature. Results are from 2019 and 2022, are consistent across epochs and with GRMHD simulations, but the interpretation of polarisation and the spin and jet details is still evolving. Confirmation by independent instrument is limited.
uncertainties: Large collaboration and diffused credit.
Limited independent confirmation and young results.
The 2020 prize for black holes may be seen as a closely related topic.
